output.classification_reasoning: The incident originates from a thread deadlock detected in the OrderFulfillmentWorker, which runs on the database-primary service. A deadlock is an application‑level concurrency bug rather than a network, authentication, or storage issue. The presence of a secondary telemetry spike indicates that the application is generating abnormal load, but the root cause remains within the application logic. Resolving a deadlock typically requires code analysis, lock ordering review, and possibly changes to transaction handling, which involves moderate effort and cross‑team coordination, placing the incident in the 'Moderate' complexity tier.

output.justification: The incident affects 800 users on a Tier-1 service and has been ongoing for 39 minutes. The governing SLA rule specifies that any Tier-1 service impact involving 500 or more users triggers a SEV-2 classification. The user count exceeds this threshold, and the outage duration is well within the window where escalation to SEV-2 is required. Therefore, the deterministic rule correctly recommends SEV-2, and no higher severity is warranted given the current impact metrics.

remediation_steps.title: Promote Read‑Replica to Primary
remediation_steps.description: Elevate the healthy read‑replica to become the new primary database to isolate the deadlocked primary instance.
verification: New primary pod reports role=primary label

remediation_steps.title: Graceful Rolling Restart of Affected Worker Pods

verification: All worker pods reach READY=1/1 within 5 minutes
kubectl logs <pod> shows no deadlock stack traces

remediation_steps.title: Post‑Remediation Health Audit
remediation_steps.description: Run synthetic health checks and verify that error rates have returned to baseline.
commands: kubectl logs -l app=order-fulfillment-worker --since=5m | grep ERR_APPLICATION_ERROR_444 || true
verification: Both health endpoints return HTTP 200 with body 'OK'

Monitoring dashboards show error rate < 1% for the last 10 minutes

rollback_plan.overall_strategy: Revert the database-primary deployment to its previous container image tag and demote the promoted replica back to read‑only mode if the new primary exhibits instability.

READY status matches pre‑remediation state

steps.description: Rollback the database-primary StatefulSet to the prior image tag.
verification: StatefulSet reports revision = previous
Pods run the previous container image

steps.description: Demote the promoted replica back to read‑only and re‑establish the original primary.
verification: Original primary pod regains role=primary label
Replica no longer reports primary status
Both primary and replica health endpoints return OK
